description: SNUPI per-motif intrinsic beam properties transcribed from Lee, Kim et al., 'Predicting the free-form shape of structured DNA assemblies from their static single-strand sequence design', ACS Nano 2021 (SNUPI), Supporting Information Tables S1-S5. Local co-rotational CR-triad beam coordinate (Notes S3-S4), 3DNA-derived then axis-converted to the beam frame. NOT Euler-ZYZ. See memory/project_snupi_mimic.md.

source.paper: SNUPI (Lee, Kim et al.), ACS Nano 2021
source.si_tables: S1 regular BP, S2 nicked BP, S3 CO-nick, S4 double CO, S5 single CO
source.notes: S3 (BP step characterization), S4 (CO step + angle correction)

convention: Quasi-harmonic Boltzmann inversion k = kB*T*F^-1 of 3DNA BP-step params, converted to beam local frame (Eq 3.17-3.22 BP, Eq 4.1-4.6 CO). Geometry split into two nodal half-values (node1,node2); for CO steps the two nodes differ by the angle correction c (Eq 4.6), so both are stored. Beam DOF order q=[dx,dy,dz,theta_x,theta_y,theta_z]; axial=dx (rise), EA is stretch along dx.

lattice_dependence.note: The 74 motif intrinsic properties are LATTICE-INDEPENDENT in SNUPI (characterized from motif MD trajectories, reused Bathe-2012 honeycomb bundles for CO motifs). Lattice type (honeycomb vs square) enters ONLY through the initial configuration, not the per-motif rigidity. Hence a single motif set, not separate HC/SQ tables. (Plan expected 'HC+SQ where they differ' — they do not differ at the motif level.)

initial_config_SI_Note_S8.rule: honeycomb = two turns per 21 bp; square = per SI Note S8
